title: The Limited Sky in the Teapot

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: So you repaired the pendant ... that's why it has these cracks?

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I wouldn't have thought it possible with just a pair of wings. Holding it at a distance, you can hardly tell it was broken.
Following his gaze down, the bird's eyes spot the jade lying on the table.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I have not checked it carefully in a very long time. Judging from the look, I might have spent a lot of effort on it indeed.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I felt something change inside me, after seeing what happened to the previous owners of the pendant. So when I left the mountain, I kept it as a reminder.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Not to meddle in others' affairs?

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: And to remind myself how similar my people and humans really are ...

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I wasn't favored by the goddess of wisdom. So please forgive me if I say anything stupid or offensive.
Softly and tentatively, he touches the edge of the pendant with his fingertips. Then he sits up.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: It feels a little like a piece of bone. Speaking of which, I wonder what you can see from my bones ... No. Never mind. I don't think I want to know.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: At first, I thought it was a trick for detecting lies and illusions. But if it's my past and future that you are seeing, count me out.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I would lose interest in living my life if I find out that I won't die surrounded by my collections of stories and beautifully carved bones.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I haven't looked that closely.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: You "haven't"! But it IS within your abilities to pry into the details. Please don't tell anyone what you see, including me. Clamp it, muzzle it! Oh ... Pardon me. I only mean your ability is very impressive. Yes. That's all I wanted to say.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: You flatter me, sir.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: But life beyond the mountain has told me much more than what the bones may tell. My people must have felt the same as they traveled across the human world.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: They thought themselves visitors to that world, only traveling through it, little did they know that they were already bound to it.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: But things are connected once they meet each other.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Novelty attracts attention, and it is all too easy to get obsessed with finding it.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I learned calligraphy, drawing, music instruments ... so many other skills. I have also learned many poems, all thanks to chasing novelty.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I started carving bones after I got this very knife.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Actually, the bone piece embedded in the blade will shine like a pearl if you put it under the light ... but there's no doubt it's bone. It even looks alive when you put it in fire ... I just can't stop looking at it.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Do your people know how to do it?

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Do what?

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Imbue things with life.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Wood, bones, metal, mud ... We may shape them into the forms of animals and men—this is one way of bringing them to life.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: The other way is ... to give them stories.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: When I first saw your bone wand and the jade pendant, I assumed that the wand was more precious than the pendant, because it has arcane power, and the pendant doesn't.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: But now, I'm more drawn in to your pendant's story.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Items with stories are more valuable than those without.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Indeed.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: And to fully master a skill, one must first find a good teacher, and then be willing to search the world to learn more ...
He stops himself.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Oh. Sorry, I should get some water. Or would you like tea? I'm going to brew some anyway.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: The branch just bought some new samovars. I'll make some tea for us.
A shiny tea set now fills up most of the space on the desk. The young man bends down to carefully light the charcoal beneath the device.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: How convenient. The pot must come from a good designer.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: My people are heavy tea-drinkers, so samovars were invented to meet our needs. It's very convenient, it pours easily and provides much needed wind protection to keep the tea warm. There's even a place to set snacks on.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: You see, no one would have been bothered to design such a thing if tea weren't introduced to us.
The glistening, amber tea is poured out of the pot until it fills the cup. As the steam rises, drops of water condense on the tips of the bird's feathers.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: If there are needs, there will be those who try to meet those needs.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: It's true, once you have a prototype, others will try to improve on it. But ...

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: The "creation" is the real exciting part.
The bird ruminates on the word.
The young man is right. His people have never developed any skills or invented anything—not even the smallest things which might make their lives easier, like this tea pot.
All they have ever done is imitation or mimicry.
They spent years learning human languages, imitating their behaviors, and adapting to their customs. The bones of their predecessors, recording all the information they would need.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Neither I nor any of my people have ever "created" anything.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: If imitation was what we left the mountain for, we probably chose the wrong path at the very beginning.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: It's meaningless.
He puts an end to this thought.
It's a conclusion he never thought he would make, but not one he never thought about before.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Don't overthink it! True invention is rare, only a small number of people ever manage it. There are as few of them as an old man's hair!

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Someone else invented it, and now all I have to do is make the tea.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Anyone can make tea.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: True, true ... but we all brew our tea a little differently. Each taste is unique.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I have to say, your dogged pursuit of an explanation reminds me of some of my other arcanist friends ...

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I don't know how to make a wand as simple and natural as yours; likewise, you can't make tea as good as mine. Things like this happen all the time. It's not a big deal.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: There's no need to dwell on the true reason you left the mountain. Maybe it was just curiosity. It could be anything!

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Or perhaps you were looking for a tool to survive.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: We don't need any new tools, my people have always had what we needed to survive.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Now, now. With that mindset, you're sure to find yourself at a dead end. How could I make tea without a samovar? You'll have to see more to know what you're capable of, what you're made to do! That's your "tool."
The young man shakes his head a little, and takes a sip from his cup. His face wrinkling up in disgust.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: *spits the tea out* It's bitter!

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Don't ... Oh, good that you haven't had any. Too many tea leaves in one pot, I'd say!

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: I'll make you another one.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: No matter. Allow me.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: ... Oh ... Well ... Thank you.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Sugar or honey?

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Honey, please. That's how we had it back in the village.
The bird nods in understanding. He stares at the tea pot and slightly lifts his wings. The bronze pot tilts as he moves, and deftly fills their cups.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Oh, and please pour my tea here, into the plate.
As he waits for his tea, the young man scoops up some honey and sends it into his mouth. Then he takes up his plate, drinking the tea from its edge.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I've never seen one drink tea in this manner before.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: You'll get used to it if you stick around. We don't have rules on how people should drink their tea here.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Indeed, it's good to learn new things.
The white steam from the hot tea rises, and they both fall into a comfortable silence.
Slowly, the steam gathers until it hangs in the air like fog. As Leonid realizes he no longer can see Gětiān's face, nor the wall behind him.
But there is still a wall, only it's no longer the staid gray office walls he knew.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: What is going on?!

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: You said you don't know anything about Artificial Somnambulism. So how did you gain access to it? You ...

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I have no such device in my possession. I spoke truly, I had never experienced its effects before.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: But I did tell you of an arcane skill similar to it. Have you forgotten?

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: It's my job to assess whether you are a threat to the Foundation. To do that, I had to keep certain information from you. We only want honest answers from you, that's all.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: Now ... You're right, we are still dreaming. That was the last piece of information I kept from you.

items.speaker: Leonid
items.text: If you're upset ...

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I knew what you wanted since the beginning.
The bird's voice is calm as he continues.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: Yet, I was bewildered by the inconsistency between your words and your deeds.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: I have also learned much from our conversation. But as I was once told, it is best to judge the heart by its deeds.

items.speaker: Yanping
items.text: ... Which is why I'm taking control.
